thread:
Priya: Quick note from a customer call -> their developer hit the sample-app and saw an "UnhandledException" even though the API returned 403 with body saying "project quota exceeded". The sample UI just showed a generic error and no hint.
Omar: Ugh. That's the py SDK transport layer mapping non-2xx to RequestError with no status/code. I think we swallow the JSON body in the exception string.
Lin: We should standardize: typed exceptions + a small flat metadata map. Minimal fields: status, code, retryable, retry_after, hint. Keep code short like "quota.project_over_daily_limit".
Priya: Yes please. For UX the sample-app should show the "hint" if present, e.g. "Upgrade your plan or contact account@redwood.ai". Make hints explicit and action-oriented.
Omar: Implementation notes: parse response JSON for a top-level "code" field and map headers Retry-After. Do not convert 4xx statuses into generic 5xx classes.
Lin: Also add a stable exception.__class__ name across SDKs (AuthError, RateLimitError, QuotaError, ClientError, ServerError, TransportError). QuotaError for 403 with quota code.
Priya: Can we include a short human message and a machine code only (no nested JSON)? Our sample-app can show the human message and ladder to help center if needed.
Omar: Agreed. And default logging should redact sensitive fields; raw body only when RI_SDK_DEBUG=true.
Lin: Telemetry: tag errors with error_class and error_code so we can alert on spikes of specific codes during onboarding flows. That should let support proactively reach out.
telemetry-bot: (automated) created ticket INF-4677: "SDK: consistent error taxonomy + sample-app hinting" assigned to Omar.
Priya: I'll take the sample-app changes (show hint and CTA for QuotaError/RateLimitError). Will update onboarding docs with suggested copy.
Omar: I'll open a py-sdk PR to add exceptions module, map statuses to classes, and ensure metadata attaches to the exception object. ETA EOW.
Lin: I'll update the SDK parity checklist and add quick unit tests for mapping and metadata presence across py/node/go.
Priya: Thanks team. Small change but should cut a lot of confusing support threads.
